clue.text: American banker in vessel with old raincoat on

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

explanation.surface: An American sits in a boat wearing an old raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword-speak for a river, something with banks, not a person who works in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing past Washington DC is a famous American watercourse, and a river is a 'banker' in crosswords.

clue.text: Place to live, above store in Cornish town

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
to stow is to store away

explanation.surface: A flat sits over a shop in a Cornish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Padstow is a fishing port on the north coast of Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip.

clue.text: 'Telegraph' work — it involved high-level performer

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of Telegraph, work and it are twisted together

explanation.surface: Working for the Telegraph involved being a high-flying performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks dress Telegraph up as the newspaper, but it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artist balancing on a wire far above the ring literally performs at a high level.

clue.text: Income assessment embarrassed statesmen

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters of statesmen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians were shamed by a check on their earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test is an official check of someone's income to decide whether they qualify for state benefits.

clue.text: Appeal of daily male!

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

explanation.surface: An exclamation about what a newspaper aimed at men offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like a newspaper; in British usage it is also a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is attractiveness, the quality that makes someone appealing.

clue.text: Bears down on printing houses

definitions.meaning: applies weight or pressure to something
publishing firms are known by the machines they print with, as in a university's publishing arm

explanation.surface: Something is putting pressure on the printing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pushes down with force; the plural noun names firms that print books, from their printing machines.

clue.text: Guard Irishman with posh car?

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is the stock Irish name in crosswords
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A security guard is an Irishman who drives a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on patrol walks the rounds watching over a place, which is what a guard does.

clue.text: Dread blowing top, making mistake

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or dread

explanation.surface: Someone full of fear loses their temper and slips up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' sounds like losing one's temper; here it removes the top letter of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a slip or blunder, the same thing as a mistake.

clue.text: Cellists forking out for small gifts

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of Cellists and forking are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cello players are paying out for little presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forking out' reads as paying, but 'forking' is fodder and 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the little presents put into a Christmas stocking.

clue.text: Conspirator against Caesar, we hear, heartless guy in combined action

indicators.note: we hear says the conspirator's name is to be taken as it sounds, 'sinner'

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators in the assassination of Julius Caesar

indicators.note: heartless means the middle goes, leaving the outer letters of guy

explanation.surface: A Roman plotter, so they say, was a heartless man taking part in a joint plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is cooperation where the combined effort exceeds the sum of the separate parts.

clue.text: Film footage randy don destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the words footage, randy and don are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A lustful university lecturer has ruined some film footage.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university lecturer; here the word is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the 1975 Sidney Lumet film starring Al Pacino as a bank robber.

clue.text: Emperor from part of Chianti, Tuscany

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An emperor comes from a corner of the Chianti region in Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor of the first century, who completed the Colosseum.

clue.text: Sail ark no more at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of ark no more are jumbled

explanation.surface: The ark has stopped being out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonraker is a small square sail set high above the skysail on a sailing ship.

clue.text: Type of bread full breakfast perhaps demands?

parts.note: whole means entire or full
breakfast is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A cooked full breakfast calls for a particular kind of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands?' just links the pieces to the definition, with a nod to the surface: a full breakfast needs bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made with flour from the entire grain, bran included, is a familiar loaf type.

clue.text: Capable, fifteen working around Channel Islands

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation
working means operating or in action, so the letters of fifteen are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A rugby fifteen playing in Jersey and Guernsey proves capable.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union side has fifteen players, which makes the surface read naturally; here the number is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficient means competent and productive, getting the job done well.

clue.text: Fine German city close to motorway

parts.note: Bonn is a German city, the former West German capital

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word motorway, its final letter

explanation.surface: A German city that sits near the autobahn is a fine place.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonny is a Scottish and northern English word for attractive or fine, as in 'a bonny day'.

clue.text: In French port, reportedly pawn fashionable brooch

indicators.note: reportedly says the port's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany, France
P is the chess notation for pawn
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Someone in a French port is said to be pawning a trendy brooch.
explanation.definitionFit: A breastpin is an ornamental pin worn on the chest, a kind of brooch.

clue.text: Worn out bagging large carp

indicators.note: bagging means capturing or pocketing, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: beat means exhausted or worn out
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An exhausted angler lands a big carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is not the fish but the verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain peevishly, and to bleat is to whine or grumble in the same way.

clue.text: Complaint undermining second-rate university in the country?

indicators.note: undermining in a down clue puts the complaint underneath the other pieces

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, below A
colic is a painful stomach complaint

explanation.surface: An illness is sapping a poor-quality university out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucolic means rural or pastoral, relating to life out in the countryside.

clue.text: Absent-minded cast, tense following Ursula's opening line

parts.note: to forge metal is to shape it, close to casting it
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word Ursula's

explanation.surface: Ursula's opening line was forgotten by the cast, who were tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' and 'line' look theatrical, but cast is a metalworking verb and line is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent-minded keeps losing track of things and fails to remember them.

clue.text: I suffer over lad's affair

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to ail is to suffer illness
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone is in pain about a young man's love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic or sexual relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Two teas before tea dance

indicators.note: before puts the first pair ahead of the last piece
Two says the slang word for tea appears twice over

parts.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea
cha is slang for tea, again

explanation.surface: Someone has a couple of cuppas before afternoon tea and a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin ballroom dance from Cuba is named for its rhythmic triple step.

clue.text: Some who telephone Claridge's, for example

indicators.note: Some means a portion of the words that follow, a run of letters hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Some people ring a smart London establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Claridge's is a famous luxury hotel in Mayfair, London.

clue.text: Impromptu remark from Democrat cornered by a Liberal

indicators.note: cornered by means trapped between, so the abbreviation sits inside the other pieces

explanation.surface: A Democrat trapped by a Liberal makes an off-the-cuff comment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad lib is something said spontaneously, without preparation or script.

clue.text: Unfortunately upset catching son dressing

indicators.note: catching means taking in, so one piece holds the other
upset means overturned, so the word for unfortunately is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone was upset to catch their son getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing ALAS gives SALA; S goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy sauce, and dressing is a general word for a sauce poured over food.

clue.text: Quick to appreciate those applauding?

definitions.meaning: a British idiom meaning very fast, as in 'running like mad'
read literally: to be fond of the people who clap

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to thank the audience for its applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is everyday British slang for very fast; read word by word it means being fond of people who clap.

clue.text: Headband: ornate relic exhibited in court

indicators.note: exhibited in means shown inside, so the shuffled letters sit within the abbreviation
ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of relic are reworked

explanation.surface: A headband, a fancy relic, is on display in a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A circlet is a small ring-shaped band worn on the head as an ornament.

clue.text: Blessing well in West African country

indicators.note: in places the word for well inside the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
so can mean well, as in 'So, what now?'

explanation.surface: A blessing comes to a well in a West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: A benison is an old literary word for a blessing or benediction.
